A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DaWin research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A.1–A.5. Text and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original DaWin experiments on ImageNet distribution shifts and eight-task model merging, together with pilot experiments, ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results, including the main benchmark tables and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The entropy-based interpolation, domain offset, mixture modeling and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Temperature scaling was already used and documented in v2; its revised description introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and its five distribution-shift benchmarks, plus the same eight multi-task datasets. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the benchmark and appendix comparisons. Table C expands labels for the existing random-uniform, WiSE-FT constant and X-entropy-ratio comparisons.

E3.justification: The added references to ID-validation temperature scaling and K=3 in Table B repeat settings already specified in v2 Sections 4.1 and A.2.3. No evaluation procedure, metric, split, model configuration or sample-size setting changes.

E4.justification: The offset, sample-size, coefficient-choice, calibration and model-pool analyses are retained with the same evidence. The rewritten discussion of Table E interprets an existing ablation; it does not introduce another experiment.

E5.justification: No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are added or revised. Table C already reported the same coefficient standard deviations; its expanded labels do not change statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Reported result entries and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, DaWin retains 78.70% ID and 54.36% OOD accuracy in Table 2 and an 86.3% multi-task average in Table 6; Tables C–G also retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The interpolation definitions, mixture-model derivations, entropy-valley hypothesis, Lemma 6.1 and Appendix A.4 proof are unchanged. Table C's expanded notation does not introduce a new mathematical result or computation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free entropy-based dynamic interpolation, efficient mixture modeling and improved robust adaptation and multi-task performance.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Table E as showing that calibration is crucial to full performance because removing it harms both ID and OOD accuracy. v3 emphasizes retained effectiveness without delicate tuning, highlighting uncalibrated DaWin's OOD advantage over WiSE-FT, 54.0% versus 51.0%. The dedicated limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: ID-validation temperature scaling and the mixture-component settings were already documented in v2 Section A.2.3. v3 repeats them in Section 3.2 and the Table B/E captions. Checkpoint, hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and positioning against static merging and training-dependent dynamic methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in Section 3.2 and the appendix calibration discussion, alongside expanded captions and labels. Section organization and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table C explicitly distinguishes standard deviations from MSE comparisons and is resized; Table D gains separators between comparator groups. Tables B and E receive expanded captions, and Table F is narrowed. Figures and table membership are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability by making existing calibration settings more prominent, labeling Table C's metrics explicitly and grouping alternatives in Table D. Table C's smaller type and reuse of lambda-star for optimal coefficients create some presentation ambiguity, but the overall clarification is useful. The experimental evidence, method and theoretical support remain unchanged.
